governance.note: Active levers all trace to measured inputs: CAMPD unit-level net-load-filtered outage windows (campd-unit-outages-PJM.csv, exogenous availability keyed on net load, not price) plus the within-window retiree CEMS availability cap (retiree_cems_cap), EIA-860 cogen-flagged BTM CHP host steam pulled out of the LP (btm.parquet: CC_CHP/CT_CHP/ST_CHP by year), measured F923 per-plant monthly delivered gas (gas_monthly_actuals + coal_plant_monthly_pricing), measured EIA-860 dual-fuel oil-parity switching, the forecast-grade reference-price interchange interface (neighbor gas x heat-rate x load-shape with a hurdle, on the priced node), grounded per-band offer-curve heat-rate multipliers from CAMPD-derived committed/peaking tranches, and the coal-BIT passthrough sigmoid. No adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to the price or volume residual; no unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled so the model output lands on actuals.
governance.btm_basis_note: First registration of pjm_38 (it was a stub: meta.json + run_config.json only, never rendered, so the scorer saw nothing/all-data-blocked). Re-solved its committed keeper config from meta.json, writing btm.parquet + the full dashboard payload + bench. CHP classes now score on the grid-delivered basis. The dominant remaining fail is the documented PJM structural coal over-run (C2 coal +13.9-22.8%) — a SEPARATE known issue (pjm-lmp-residual / pjm-coal-mustrun-floor), the forecast-native consequence the net-load outage re-gate amplified, NOT a BTM artifact and NOT folded into this re-gate.
